paragraphs: Active learning asks which questions a learner should pose when labels are expensive. Here, the learner has a fixed collection of unlabeled examples and wants to label them nearly as well as the best rule in a chosen class. The paper focuses on halfspaces, which classify examples by placing a linear boundary between groups.

Ordinary label queries can require a number of questions proportional to the inverse of the desired error. Earlier, more expressive questions greatly reduced that dependence when a halfspace labeled everything perfectly, but became fragile with noise. The authors introduce threshold statistical queries and prove an efficient algorithm under Massart noise. At noise rate η, it produces a labeling with error at most η + ε using only polylogarithmically many queries in 1/ε and polynomial computation time.

The paper also establishes a boundary for this improvement. Under the more permissive agnostic noise model, inverse-error query complexity remains unavoidable, even for a simpler function class. The benefit therefore depends on the noise structure, rather than holding for arbitrary labeling errors.
neurips-2024-active-classification-with-.tldr: Threshold statistical queries enable efficient halfspace learning under Massart noise, while stronger agnostic noise prevents comparable query savings.

paragraphs: A vision-language model learning new domains has two responsibilities: retain what it learns along the way and preserve its ability to recognize things in domains it has never encountered. Existing approaches described in the paper need extra reference data to protect that original ability, and domain labels to help classify incoming images.

RAIL addresses these requirements with an adapter based on recursive ridge regression. It updates the learned mapping as domains arrive and projects features into a larger space to separate cross-domain correlations. A fusion component that needs no training combines with this adapter. The authors state that this arrangement fully preserves zero-shot ability on unseen domains without reference data, and they theoretically establish absolute memorization of incrementally learned domains.

The paper also introduces X-TAIL, an evaluation setting where test images can come from seen or unseen domains without identifying their domain. RAIL achieves the reported best performance in this setting and in existing multi-domain task-incremental evaluations. This makes preserving knowledge and handling unknown domain identity part of the same learning problem.
neurips-2024-advancing-cross-domain-disc.tldr: RAIL incrementally learns domains while preserving zero-shot ability and classifying images without domain-identity hints.

paragraphs: Stereotypes in generated images can arise from relationships between objects, even when prompts mentioning those objects separately do not reveal the same bias. The paper studies this association-level problem. Its example concerns the increased association of Black people with poorer housing when people and houses appear together in a prompt.

The proposed MAS framework treats mitigation as aligning probability distributions. It aims to bring the distribution of stereotypes in generated images toward a stereotype-free target distribution. One component, PIS CLIP, learns relationships among prompts, images, and stereotypes, creating a way to connect a prompt with the stereotypes it may evoke. A Sensitive Transformer then produces constraints that guide the generated distribution toward the target.

The authors also introduce SDTV, a measure designed to evaluate association-engendered stereotypes because existing measures do not adequately capture them. Experiments show that MAS mitigates these stereotypes. The contribution is to make combinations of depicted objects an explicit target of both intervention and evaluation, extending beyond approaches focused on individual objects.
neurips-2024-association-of-objects-may-.tldr: MAS reduces stereotypes arising from object associations by guiding generated-image distributions toward a stereotype-free target.

paragraphs: Vision-language models can produce fluent answers that conflict with the image they were given. The paper attributes this misalignment to models placing too much weight on text, even when their language and visual components are individually strong. Collecting preference examples with extra models or human annotations can be expensive and may poorly reflect the target model's own preferences.

Calibrated Self-Rewarding, or CSR, builds an iterative improvement loop around the model itself. The model generates possible responses, scores them, and uses the resulting preferences for further tuning. Its scoring process works step by step and incorporates visual constraints, making image evidence more influential when deciding which responses deserve higher rewards.

Across twelve benchmarks and tasks, the authors report better performance and fewer hallucinations, including a reported 7.62% improvement over existing methods. They also provide theoretical support for introducing visual constraints under mild assumptions. Results across different vision-language models and successive tuning rounds suggest that the approach can support incremental improvement through repeated self-evaluation.
neurips-2024-calibrated-self-rewarding-v.tldr: CSR helps vision-language models improve themselves by grounding their self-generated training preferences more strongly in image evidence.

paragraphs: 3D Gaussian Splatting represents scenes with many Gaussian elements and their attributes, enabling fast, detailed rendering from new viewpoints. Those elements also create a substantial storage burden. The paper identifies a missed compression opportunity: methods that encode neural Gaussians independently make little use of their spatial relationships.

ContextGS organizes anchors into levels and encodes them in an order that exposes useful context. Anchors still awaiting encoding are predicted using anchors already encoded at coarser levels. Better predictions make the remaining information cheaper to store. The method also gives each anchor a small quantized feature, called a hyperprior, to improve entropy coding. This is particularly useful at the coarsest level, where previously encoded anchors are unavailable.

The authors report representations over 100 times smaller than ordinary 3D Gaussian Splatting and 15 times smaller than Scaffold-GS, with comparable or better rendering quality. The central finding is that modeling relationships among anchors can substantially improve compression while preserving the scene information needed for high-quality views.
neurips-2024-contextgs-compact-3d-gaussi.tldr: ContextGS compresses Gaussian scenes by predicting anchors from coarser context, achieving large storage reductions with comparable or better rendering quality.

paragraphs: Visual simultaneous localization and mapping estimates a camera's pose while building a representation of its surroundings. Gaussian Splatting has improved the visual quality of these representations, but the systems discussed in this paper assume that the environment is static. Moving scene content introduces inconsistencies in geometry and appearance that make camera tracking harder.

DG-SLAM adapts this approach to dynamic environments while retaining an explicit representation built from 3D Gaussians. It combines motion-mask generation, adaptive management of Gaussian points, and a hybrid camera-tracking algorithm. These components address the challenge of estimating camera motion when the observations also contain movement within the scene. The objective covers both accurate localization and detailed reconstruction.

The reported experiments show state-of-the-art performance for camera pose estimation, map reconstruction, and rendering new viewpoints in dynamic scenes. The system also preserves real-time rendering capability. These findings connect tracking robustness with reconstruction quality: the proposed system improves both in the moving environments evaluated, rather than treating visually detailed maps as sufficient evidence of reliable localization.
neurips-2024-dg-slam-robust-dynamic-gaus.tldr: DG-SLAM combines motion handling and hybrid camera tracking to improve Gaussian-based mapping and localization in dynamic scenes.

paragraphs: Spiking neural networks communicate through binary spikes, allowing many multiplications to be replaced by additions. That makes them attractive for efficient computation, but binary feature maps restrict what they can represent. This paper asks whether enriching the feature vector immediately before classification can improve their accuracy, as richer output features do in conventional neural networks.

The authors propose two changes. First, they use a trained conventional network to guide the spiking network. Features from both networks pass through the conventional network's classifier, and a KL-divergence loss aligns the resulting outputs. This uses the trained classifier's information to shape feature learning. Second, they replace the final spiking activation with ReLU, producing a full-precision output feature with only a small increase in computation.

Ablation studies find the proposed alignment loss more effective than ordinary knowledge distillation. Across the tested static-image and neuromorphic datasets, the combined method consistently outperforms the compared state-of-the-art algorithms. The findings support improving the representation at the classification interface as a practical route to more accurate spiking networks.
neurips-2024-enof-snn-training-accurate-.tldr: EnOF-SNN improves spiking-network accuracy through classifier-guided distillation and a full-precision feature representation before classification.

paragraphs: Diffusion MRI records a directional signal inside each voxel, describing how strongly water diffuses along different directions. Analyzing it therefore requires handling both where a measurement sits in the brain and how its signal varies across a sphere. The paper develops neural-network layers that explicitly respect the physical symmetries of these data.

The layers are equivariant to spatial rotations, translations, and reflections, together with rotations of directional signals within individual voxels. Equivariance means that transformed inputs lead to correspondingly transformed outputs. The authors also exploit the typical antipodal symmetry of neuronal fibers, where opposite directions describe the same fiber orientation. This allows efficient graph convolutions using hemispherical structure.

The method is applied to sparse spherical fiber deconvolution, which recovers information about white-matter structure. Experiments on simulated data and in vivo human data consistently show gains in performance and efficiency. These gains improve the practical resolution of crossing fibers and fiber tractography, connecting the network's symmetry-aware design to the anatomical structures the analysis seeks to recover.
neurips-2024-equivariant-spatio-hemisphe.tldr: Symmetry-aware hemispherical network layers improve the accuracy and efficiency of recovering fiber structure from diffusion MRI.

paragraphs: Generalization bounds help relate a model's behavior on training data to its behavior beyond those data. This paper develops bounds using conditional f-information, a broader framework than conditional mutual information. Its approach operates in the supersample setting and accommodates both bounded and unbounded loss functions, extending the kinds of losses covered.

The main technical change concerns how the proof handles the cumulant-generating function in an information-theoretic variational formula. Earlier mutual-information arguments upper-bound this quantity. Here, the authors carefully choose the measurable function in the formula so that the quantity, or its upper bound, becomes zero. Although some ideas draw inspiration from coin-betting research, the results do not depend on prior regret guarantees for online gambling algorithms.

A new mutual-information bound recovers many earlier results and helps clarify their potential limitations. The authors also compare different f-information measures empirically and report improved bounds over previous ones. The contribution therefore includes a general proof strategy, a connection to established bounds, and evidence that the broader framework can yield tighter assessments.
neurips-2024-generalization-bounds-via-c.tldr: Conditional f-information provides a broader route to generalization bounds, with a new proof strategy and reported improvements over earlier bounds.

paragraphs: A segmentation model operating in an open world must respond differently to two kinds of unfamiliarity. A known category may appear under a new domain's visual conditions, where the model should still recognize it. An entirely new category instead calls for anomaly detection. Existing methods can confuse these shifts, weakening either generalization or detection.

The paper trains the model to distinguish these cases using generated augmentation images. These images coherently combine novel objects with changes in appearance at both the whole-image and individual-object levels. The training strategy then recalibrates uncertainty specifically for semantic changes while encouraging the feature extractor to align representations associated with domain changes.

Across the evaluated benchmarks containing both types of shift, the method achieves the reported best performance for out-of-distribution detection and domain generalization. The stated result matters because the two objectives are addressed together. The approach aims to preserve confidence when familiar content changes appearance while making uncertainty informative when the category itself is outside the model's known semantics.
neurips-2024-generalize-or-detect-toward.tldr: Joint augmentation and targeted training help segmentation models generalize across domains while detecting genuinely novel categories.

paragraphs: Recognizing every object in an image can benefit from relationships among labels, but those relationships may reflect biased training contexts. A classifier can then rely on associations that fail during testing. This paper revisits label correlations through causal intervention, seeking to retain useful context while suppressing misleading associations rather than removing contextual information altogether.

A Transformer decoder first separates features associated with individual labels. The method also clusters spatial features across the training images to model confounders that may produce spurious relationships. A cross-attention component combines the label-specific features and modeled confounders to implement the intervention, estimating causal correlations from all object categories to each category being predicted.

Final labels combine predictions from the separated features with predictions informed by the causal correlations. Experiments support the approach in both ordinary evaluations and cross-dataset settings. The findings suggest that the usefulness of label relationships depends on how they are modeled: accounting for possible confounding can make context beneficial without simply accepting all observed co-occurrence as reliable evidence.
neurips-2024-in-pursuit-of-causal-label-.tldr: The method uses causal intervention to exploit useful label relationships while reducing spurious contextual associations in multi-label recognition.

paragraphs: Large text-to-image models can require expensive GPUs and substantial memory, limiting access and reproducibility. KOALA investigates how much generation capability can be retained in smaller models using publicly available data and open-source models. Stable Diffusion XL serves as the starting point for studying how to transfer capability into a compact U-Net.

The study identifies three practices. In knowledge distillation, self-attention is the most important component examined. For data, high-resolution images paired with detailed captions matter more than a larger collection of low-resolution images with short captions. Using a teacher already distilled for fewer generation steps also helps the smaller model reduce its step count.

These findings lead to KOALA-Turbo and KOALA-Lightning variants with one-billion- and 700-million-parameter U-Nets. KOALA-Lightning-700M is reported to run four times faster than SDXL while retaining satisfactory generation quality. The models can also generate 1024-pixel images on an 8 GB consumer GPU. Together, the results provide an empirical recipe for making high-resolution generation more accessible under limited hardware resources.
neurips-2024-koala-empirical-lessons-tow.tldr: KOALA uses targeted distillation, richer training data, and efficient teachers to deliver faster, smaller text-to-image models.

paragraphs: Resolving a GitHub issue requires working within an existing repository, where a solution must both add appropriate code and maintain what is already there. Language models can generate code, yet this broader task remains difficult. The authors begin by empirically examining why models fail at issue resolution and identifying major contributing factors.

Those findings motivate MAGIS, a framework that distributes work among four specialized agents: a Manager, Repository Custodian, Developer, and Quality Assurance Engineer. Their collaboration spans planning and coding. The framework organizes model capabilities around software-evolution responsibilities, making coordination among roles part of the proposed solution to repository-level work.

On SWE-bench, MAGIS resolves 13.94% of issues and substantially exceeds the compared language-model baselines, which include GPT-3.5, GPT-4, and Claude-2. Its resolved proportion is eight times that of directly applying GPT-4. These results support coordinated agents as a useful approach in the evaluated setting, while the absolute success rate also shows that successful repository-level resolution remains far from routine.
neurips-2024-magis-llm-based-multi-agent.tldr: MAGIS coordinates four specialized agents to resolve GitHub issues, achieving 13.94% success on SWE-bench.

paragraphs: Reconstructing video from fMRI requires recovering a continuous visual experience, including both its meaning and how its appearance changes over time. NeuroClips builds on the view that high-level semantics and low-level perceptual flows must both be decoded accurately. This separates two demands that a reconstruction must satisfy: recognizable content and smooth temporal behavior.

A semantics reconstructor produces video keyframes to guide content accuracy and consistency. A separate perception reconstructor captures lower-level visual details associated with smoothness. During inference, the framework supplies both keyframes and perceptual flows to a pretrained text-to-video diffusion model, which uses them to generate the reconstructed sequence.

On a public fMRI-video dataset, NeuroClips reconstructs videos lasting up to six seconds at eight frames per second. The authors report improvements over state-of-the-art models, including 128% in SSIM and 81% in spatiotemporal metrics. These measured gains support the framework's division of semantic and perceptual decoding as a way to improve both fidelity and temporal quality in the evaluated reconstruction task.
neurips-2024-neuroclips-towards-high-fid.tldr: NeuroClips combines decoded keyframes and perceptual flows to reconstruct more faithful, smoother videos from fMRI.

paragraphs: Online learning must adapt as losses arrive, and a changing environment makes success harder to measure than comparison with one fixed decision. This paper studies non-convex losses using dynamic regret and adaptive regret. These criteria assess performance against changing comparators and over time intervals, extending earlier guarantees for follow the perturbed leader in static environments.

The first algorithm, FTPL-D, periodically restarts the underlying learner. With prior knowledge of total loss variation V_T, it achieves dynamic regret O(T^(2/3)(V_T + 1)^(1/3)). When that variation is unknown, the method runs learners with different restart choices and tracks them using a meta-algorithm. Randomized sampling addresses the difficulty of combining experts under non-convex losses.

A second algorithm, FTPL-A, dynamically maintains FTPL experts and achieves adaptive regret O(√(τ log T)) on any interval of length τ. It also obtains a dynamic-regret bound of the same stated order up to logarithmic factors. The paper discusses online constrained meta-learning and reports experiments supporting the methods, connecting the theoretical guarantees to adaptation in changing learning problems.
neurips-2024-online-non-convex-learning-.tldr: Restarted and dynamically combined FTPL learners provide regret guarantees for online non-convex learning in changing environments.

paragraphs: Evaluating a computer assistant requires more than checking whether it can describe a screen or operate one specialized application. OSWorld provides an interactive environment for tasks across real applications and operating systems, including Ubuntu, Windows, and macOS. It supports task setup, execution-based evaluation, and interactive learning within a shared framework.

The accompanying benchmark contains 369 tasks drawn from real computer use. They involve web and desktop applications, file operations, and workflows that cross application boundaries. Each task includes a specified starting configuration and a custom script that evaluates what the agent actually accomplished. These provisions are intended to make assessments reliable and reproducible across complex computer workflows.

The evaluation reveals a substantial gap between people and the tested agents. Humans complete over 72.36% of tasks, whereas the best model reaches 12.24%. The main reported difficulties concern grounding actions in graphical interfaces and knowing how to operate applications. OSWorld therefore supplies both a broader testing environment and concrete evidence about where current computer-assistant capabilities break down.
neurips-2024-osworld-benchmarking-multim.tldr: OSWorld evaluates agents on 369 real computer tasks and exposes a large performance gap between humans and tested models.

paragraphs: Distributionally robust optimization prepares a model for uncertainty about its data distribution. It optimizes performance against the worst distribution inside a specified ambiguity set. How that set is defined therefore matters: it determines which distribution changes the model must withstand. This paper develops a definition intended to be more resilient to outliers.

The proposed distance is inspired by unbalanced optimal transport and uses a soft penalty in place of hard constraints. That change produces an ambiguity set with improved outlier resilience. Under smoothness conditions, the authors establish strong duality for the resulting optimization problem. They also introduce a computationally efficient Lagrangian penalty formulation and show that strong duality holds for it as well.

Experiments on regression and classification report improved robustness to outliers together with lower computational demands. The work thus links the statistical choice of a distributional distance to the tractability of the resulting optimization. Its theoretical equivalences are conditional on the stated smoothness requirements, while the practical robustness and efficiency improvements are demonstrated empirically.
neurips-2024-outlier-robust-distribution.tldr: A soft-penalty transport distance yields distributionally robust optimization with improved empirical outlier resistance and computational efficiency.

paragraphs: Many adversarial attacks on vision-language models depend on knowledge of model internals or require separate perturbations for different tasks. This paper investigates a more general threat: a reusable visual patch developed using only model inputs and outputs. The goal is to influence behavior across varied inputs, tasks, and prompts without inspecting the model's architecture.

The approach initially samples patch locations and patterns, using the semantic relationship between model responses and a target label to guide the search. It then fixes the location and refines the pattern. Diverse task inputs supply queries for estimating how the patch should change, with different inputs contributing according to their importance.

Experiments on LLaVA, MiniGPT-4, Flamingo, and BLIP-2 demonstrate strong adversarial effects across the evaluated tasks and prompts. The significance is the combination of restricted access and broad patch reuse: the attack does not require internal gradients or structural details. Although universality is the design objective, the reported evidence establishes effectiveness across the models and tasks tested.
neurips-2024-pandora-s-box-towards-build.tldr: The paper develops reusable adversarial patches that affect multiple vision-language tasks using only model input-output access.

paragraphs: Classification with rejection lets a model abstain when making a prediction is undesirable. A common approach builds that choice into supervised training by assigning rejection a smaller penalty than an incorrect answer. This paper instead starts with a pretrained model and asks what data distribution would make that model perform best.

The authors formalize that question by optimizing expected loss while regularizing the proposed distribution with a φ-divergence term. The regularizer constrains the search through a measure of distributional difference. Once an idealized distribution is obtained, the method uses its density ratio relative to the original data distribution to decide whether to reject a prediction. This makes distributional weighting the basis of abstention.

The study concentrates on the α-divergence family and evaluates the framework on both clean and noisy datasets. Its central contribution is a different formulation of rejection around an existing predictor. The abstract reports empirical testing, but makes no specific comparative performance claim; the stated result is the framework and its evaluation across these data conditions.
neurips-2024-rejection-via-learning-dens.tldr: The framework decides when a pretrained classifier should abstain by comparing the data distribution with an idealized distribution favoring its performance.

paragraphs: Editing a language model aims to change particular responses without retraining the entire system or disturbing its other behavior. This paper develops theoretical foundations for such selective changes. It identifies a measure of the intrinsic dimension of model features that helps assess editability and predict the success of several editing approaches.

The analysis connects editing methods that had appeared separate and guides the design of a new insertable network block called a jet-pack. Built from standard network operations, this block is optimized for highly selective editing. The intended corrective use is to alter responses to known prompts that produce hallucinations while leaving other model behavior unaffected.

The same selectivity also exposes a vulnerability: a small weight modification can set a response to an attacker-chosen prompt. The authors report that these attacks are computationally simple and need neither access to nor knowledge of training data. Experiments support the methods and theory, showing how a mechanism useful for targeted correction can also threaten redistributed foundation models.
neurips-2024-stealth-edits-to-large-lang.tldr: A theory of selective model editing enables targeted corrections while revealing how small weight changes can implant attacker-chosen responses.

paragraphs: Concept bottleneck models make predictions through intermediate concepts that people can understand and correct. This gives users a direct way to intervene when a model misinterprets an input, but correcting concepts manually takes time. The paper asks how to make each correction more effective by accounting for dependencies among concepts.

Stochastic Concept Bottleneck Models represent these dependencies explicitly through a probability distribution. Correcting one concept can therefore affect other correlated concepts as well. The distributional representation preserves efficient training and inference, unlike approaches that organize concept relationships through an autoregressive structure. The authors also use this parameterization to derive an intervention strategy based on a confidence region.

Experiments with synthetic tabular data and natural images show significantly improved intervention effectiveness. The paper additionally examines concepts inferred by CLIP, reducing the need for manually supplied concept annotations. Together, these results show how modeling relationships within the interpretable layer can increase the value of human corrections while supporting a setting where the concepts themselves are obtained automatically.
neurips-2024-stochastic-concept-bottlene.tldr: Stochastic concept bottleneck models use concept dependencies to make individual human corrections more effective.

paragraphs: Boosting combines relatively inaccurate classifiers into a more accurate voting predictor. This paper focuses on achieving that improvement with provably optimal sample complexity: using training examples as efficiently as the theoretical problem permits. Algorithms with this guarantee had only recently become available, motivating a simpler and faster way to obtain it.

The proposed procedure is straightforward. Split the training data into five equally sized, disjoint subsets, run AdaBoost separately on each subset, and combine the five resulting classifiers by majority vote. The authors prove that this construction achieves optimal sample complexity. They also establish the fastest runtime among the sample-optimal boosting algorithms considered, pairing the statistical guarantee with a computational advantage.

The paper additionally presents the first empirical comparison of the proposed sample-optimal boosting algorithms. Its pilot study suggests that the new method might outperform earlier algorithms on large datasets. This practical conclusion is deliberately tentative: the strongest claims concern the proved sample complexity and runtime, while the observed performance advantage remains a finding from an initial empirical study.
neurips-2024-the-many-faces-of-optimal-w.tldr: A majority vote over five separately trained AdaBoost classifiers achieves provably optimal sample complexity with a simple, fast procedure.

paragraphs: Diffusion Transformers generate images in latent space using sequences of transformer blocks. This paper revisits the decision to move away from U-Net architectures. In a preliminary comparison, giving a diffusion transformer a U-shaped architecture produces only a small advantage, suggesting that the resulting design may contain redundancy despite its useful structural bias.

The authors connect this redundancy to the observation that U-Net features are dominated by low-frequency information. They downsample the tokens used for the query, key, and value components of self-attention. This reduces computation substantially while also improving performance. The resulting attention mechanism forms the basis of a family of U-shaped Diffusion Transformers called U-DiTs.

Extensive experiments support the proposed models, including a reported result that a U-DiT can outperform DiT-XL using one-sixth of its computation. The finding goes beyond simply restoring a U-shaped backbone: the gains come from adapting attention to the feature structure within that backbone. In the evaluated setting, reducing token-level computation improves both efficiency and generation performance.
neurips-2024-u-dits-downsample-tokens-in.tldr: U-DiTs downsample attention tokens in U-shaped diffusion transformers, outperforming DiT-XL in a reported comparison at one-sixth of its computation.

paragraphs: Mamba's selective state-space architecture has attracted attention for visual tasks, but its internal behavior and the best ways to improve it remain active questions. Existing visual adaptations often change scanning patterns or combine architectures using predefined design choices. This paper proposes a systematic process for diagnosing problems before choosing how to repair them.

Vision Mamba Mender analyzes predictive correlations in hidden states from both internal and external perspectives. It defines corresponding correlation scores to investigate how the model works in visual recognition and to locate flaws in those states. The framework then applies repair methods tailored to the internal or external flaws that the analysis identifies.

Experiments across prevalent Mamba architectures show significant performance improvements and support the proposed analysis and repair methods. The contribution is therefore both diagnostic and practical: it offers measurements intended to reveal weaknesses, followed by targeted modifications intended to address them. The reported gains indicate that inspecting hidden-state behavior can provide a productive basis for improving the tested vision models.
neurips-2024-vision-mamba-mender-4919873.tldr: Vision Mamba Mender diagnoses hidden-state flaws through correlation analysis and applies targeted repairs that improve visual recognition performance.

paragraphs: Visually grounded language models can perform worse at basic image classification than CLIP, even when they use CLIP as their visual encoder and contain many more parameters. This paper investigates that gap in proprietary and public models, including GPT-4V and LLaVA, by examining inference procedures, training objectives, and data processing.

The analysis identifies data as the main cause. Information needed for classification is present in the model's latent representation, but sufficient training data are needed to decode it effectively. Class-level performance strongly correlates with how often each class appears during training and instruction tuning. With enough training data, the studied models can match state-of-the-art classification accuracy.

Guided by these findings, the authors add classification-focused datasets to a vision-language model's training. The resulting improvement extends to broader capabilities, with an 11.8% gain on their newly collected ImageWikiQA dataset. The results point to class exposure and effective use of existing visual information as important factors in the classification gap, rather than model size alone explaining capability.
neurips-2024-why-are-visually-grounded-l.tldr: The study links weak image classification in vision-language models primarily to training-data exposure and improves performance with classification-focused training.
